previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease, bilateral lower extremity amputations, and a history of recurrent C. difficile infections was admitted after being found unresponsive by EMS. She had severe hypoglycemia with a blood glucose of 16, likely due to an insulin dosing error, and was treated with dextrose via her dialysis line. She also presented with hypotension and dehydration, thought to be secondary to recent C. difficile colitis and inadequate oral intake. Stool testing confirmed toxigenic C. difficile, and she was started on a tapered course of oral vancomycin. Initial concern for a multidrug-resistant urinary tract infection led to empiric antibiotics, but these were discontinued when cultures showed low bacterial counts and no signs of sepsis. Her dialysis catheter was replaced prior to discharge as a preventive measure. She remained hemodynamically stable, restarted her heart medications, and was discharged home in improved condition with medication adjustments and close follow-up planned.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

You were admitted to ___ for facial swelling.  We are not sure 
what caused this swelling, but it may have been a result of 
taking Mirtazipine (Remeron). We suggest that you stop taking 
this medication. This swelling is called angioedema. You were 
treated with prednisone and your symptoms completely resolved.  
You should continue to take prednisone for the next 5 days.  

If your swelling worsens or you develop difficulty breathing, 
please return to the hospital immediately.  Please do not take 
Mirtazipine anymore, and discuss starting a different 
anti-depressant with your primary doctor and psychiatrist.

FINDINGS:

Frontal and lateral views of the chest were obtained.  Large bore central
catheter terminates in the right atrium, in similar position to prior.  IVC
filter has a stable orientation.  Heart size and cardiomediastinal contours
are normal.  Linear opacity in the right mid lung is unchanged and consistent
with atelectasis.  No focal consolidation, pneumothorax, or substantial
pleural effusion.  

IMPRESSION:

No acute cardiopulmonary process.  This exam neither suggests nor excludes the
diagnosis of pulmonary embolism.
